title: Delhi Building Collapse Kills Child, Traps Several as Rescue Continues in Seemapuri
excerpt: The front portion of a four-storey building in New Seemapuri came down around 3:30 pm on Wednesday, killing a five-year-old and injuring at least seven; residents say cracks appeared after Tuesday night's Uttarakhand earthquake tremors.
body:
• The front portion of a four-storey building collapsed in New Seemapuri, northeast Delhi, on Wednesday afternoon around 3:30 pm; a child aged about five was killed and at least seven people, including a three-year-old, were injured.
  • Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police, civil defence personnel and civic officials rushed to the site near Eidgah Fish Market, where heavy machinery and local residents were clearing rubble by hand; several people are still feared trapped.
  • What readers in Delhi need to know: traffic is affected around Seemapuri Gol Chakkar, DLF Bhopura and adjoining roads — Delhi Traffic Police has urged commuters to avoid the area and keep lanes clear for ambulances and rescue vehicles.
  • Some residents linked the collapse to cracks that appeared after Tuesday night's 4.9-magnitude Uttarakhand earthquake, whose tremors shook Delhi-NCR; officials say the cause will be determined by investigation.

A multi-storey building collapsed in northeast Delhi's New Seemapuri area on Wednesday afternoon, killing a child aged around five and leaving at least seven people injured, with several others feared trapped under the debris, PTI reported.

The Delhi Fire Service received a call around 3:30 pm about the front portion of the four-storey building collapsing. Fire tenders were rushed to the spot, while Delhi Police, civic officials and civil defence personnel joined the search and rescue operation. The child's body was recovered from the rubble; at least seven people, including a three-year-old child, were pulled out injured.

"We received information at 3:40 PM. This is a four-storey building, which is 25 square yards in area. So far, 7 people have been rescued. They are out of danger. The rescue operation is ongoing... All agencies are present at the scene; ambulances and Delhi Fire Service staff are deployed. MCD officials, DM, everyone is present at the scene," Shahdara DCP Rajendra Prasad Meena told ANI.

Rescue under way

The collapsed structure measured around 225 square feet, and debris also buried portions of two to three adjoining houses, according to the DCP. Rescue teams deployed heavy machinery, including JCB excavators, to clear large piles of bricks, stones and debris near Eidgah Fish Market.

https://x.com/WIONews/status/2107798846911000759

Visuals from the spot showed local residents joining the rescue effort, clearing rubble with their bare hands. In one video, a group of people could be seen pulling a woman out from under the debris and carrying her away in their arms. Paramedics attended to the rescued and shifted the injured to hospitals.

One local resident said locals had rescued four to five people before police arrived: "Police came after half an hour. There is a child still trapped, and some have been rescued by people and sent to hospitals. I have given CPR myself," he said. Others were seen crying near the collapse site as the search continued.

Locals link collapse to earthquake tremors

Some residents claimed the building had developed cracks after tremors were felt across Delhi-NCR following a 4.9-magnitude earthquake in Uttarakhand on Tuesday night. One family member told reporters the building had been evacuated after the earthquake, but residents were gradually returning when it suddenly collapsed around 3:30 pm.

Officials, however, said the actual cause of the collapse would be ascertained only after an investigation — a familiar refrain in a city where unauthorized construction and weak enforcement repeatedly turn structural failures into mass-casualty events.

Context: a deadly pattern

The Seemapuri collapse comes barely a month after a five-storey paying-guest building collapsed in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven students and injuring 12 others. Five people, including building owner Hariram Gupta, were detained in connection with that incident.

Two multi-storey collapses in the capital within five weeks — both in densely packed residential pockets — point to a systemic problem: ageing and often illegally extended structures in neighborhoods where building codes exist mostly on paper, and where residents have little recourse until the rubble falls.

What's next

The rescue operation was continuing into the evening, with authorities yet to confirm the final casualty count or the number of people still trapped. A structural investigation will determine whether the earthquake tremors were a trigger, a coincidence, or a convenient explanation for a building that was already failing.
